who: Hippocratic Aphorisms II.49 · tr. Francis Adams, 1849
quote: Those who are accustomed to endure habitual labors, although they be weak or old, bear them better than strong and young persons who have not been so accustomed.
meaning: Old people who move every day handle hard work better than strong young people who don't.

who: Wu Pu, student of the physician Hua Tuo · Sanguozhi, tr. from Chinese
quote: Wu Pu learned Hua Tuo's Five Animals exercise: tiger, deer, bear, ape and bird. The old history says he practised it, and at over ninety his hearing and sight were sharp and his teeth whole and firm.
meaning: The old history says the student who did these animal moves stayed sharp past ninety.

who: Galen · On Health V.4, tr. P. N. Singer, 2023
quote: Galen tells of Antiochus, a doctor past eighty, who walked daily from home to the town square and visited nearby patients on foot. Through this routine he ‘continued right to the end with his senses unimpaired and his limbs supple.’
meaning: A doctor over eighty walked every day and still saw patients. His body stayed supple.

who: Socrates · Xenophon, Symposium 2.16-19, tr. H. G. Dakyns, 1897
quote: Socrates asked to learn the dance steps, and everyone laughed. He replied: ‘Pray, do you find it so ridiculous my wishing to improve my health by exercise?...’
meaning: Wanting to move more at any age is never silly. It is good for your health.

who: Kaibara Ekiken · Yojokun, 1713 · tr. from Japanese
quote: In his eighties, finishing his health book, Kaibara Ekiken wrote: ‘Now, at eighty-three, I still write and read small characters at night; my teeth are firm and not one has fallen out.’
meaning: He lived by his own advice. In his eighties he was still reading and writing at night.

who: Russian proverb · V. I. Dal's collection, 1862
quote: Old, but sturdy. Both fresh and fit.
meaning: You can be old and still strong, fresh and ready.

quote: In 1950, when Krishnamacharya was about 60, his yoga school in Mysore closed and he had to start over. He moved to Chennai, taught new students, healthy and sick, for decades, and turned 100 there in November 1988.
meaning: At about 60 he had to start again. He kept teaching and reached 100.

who: B. K. S. Iyengar · to Yoga Journal, 2008
quote: Even now, the maximum my body can do, I do. I am 90, and still I practice. I stay in Sirsasana (Headstand) for half an hour, even without shaking. I'm improving still, progressing still.
meaning: At 90 he still practised every day and felt he was still getting better.

quote: In 2012, aged 93, Tao Porchon-Lynch was named the world's oldest yoga teacher by Guinness World Records, still teaching four days a week. ‘I believe that we can always reach just a little bit further.’
meaning: At 93 she still taught four days a week and kept reaching a little further.

quote: The Guardian wrote of Pattabhi Jois: ‘Up every morning to start classes at 5am, he rarely missed a day's teaching in 70 years.’ He taught at his own school until 2008, into his nineties.
meaning: Our Ashtanga comes from a teacher who showed up every morning for 70 years.
